display_name: The Ledger of the Lantern Tide

clergy.vestments: sea-green mantles over white coats, trimmed with copper chain and shell seals
clergy.holy_symbol: a lantern hanging above a wave-mark

cosmology.opposing_view_detail: Chaotic powers are named deepwater demons that delight in shipwreck, mutiny, broken contracts, and drowned memory.
cosmology.notes: See §3.3 Alignment Cosmology Rules for the hard constraints governing this field.

pantheon.holy_symbol: a lantern above three wave lines
pantheon.domains_summary: Thalor rules lawful commerce at sea, safe harbors, and the beacons that lead vessels home.

pantheon.holy_symbol: a knotted cord over a water drop
pantheon.domains_summary: Meras judges contracts, tolls, and chance upon the water, rewarding honest reckoning.

pantheon.holy_symbol: a fish basket beneath an open hand
pantheon.domains_summary: Velis blesses shared plenty, dockside relief, and the mutual aid that keeps ports alive.

pantheon.holy_symbol: a crescent over a masthead eye
pantheon.domains_summary: Orun grants charts, celestial knowledge, and the disciplined patience required for long voyages.

flavor_text.one_line: A maritime faith of beacon-law, honest contracts, and shared rescue beneath the lanterns.
flavor_text.one_paragraph: The Ledger teaches that the sea is survivable only when people hold to witnessed duty: pilot to ship, city to sailor, wealthy guild to hungry dock, and captain to charter. While Thalor is honored above the other powers, the whole lantern-tide is venerated through harbor rites, rescue funds, and public accounting of wreck losses. Chaotic forces are cast as abyssal demons that thrive on mutiny, hidden cargo, and the deliberate extinguishing of guiding lights.
flavor_text.creation_myth_summary: When the first coast drowned in darkness, Thalor raised lanterns from the surf and taught mortals to mark depth, debt, and safe return.
flavor_text.moral_code_summary: Honor contracts, aid the shipwrecked, pay due tithe, keep public lights burning, and resist Chaos in mutiny, piracy, and fraudulent gain.
